rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
Correlates Akeso AV quarantine events with Akeso DLP classification
or policy violation events involving the same file. When a file that was
previously flagged by DLP as containing sensitive data is later quarantined
by AV, this indicates malware specifically targeting sensitive documents —
a high-confidence indicator of targeted data theft.
rules.name: AV + DLP - Malware Targeting Sensitive Documents
AV + DLP Malware Targeting Sensitive Data Correlation

rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
Three-stage cross-source temporal correlation:
1. EDR detects credential theft (LSASS access, mimikatz, sekurlsa)
2. NDR detects lateral movement (SMB write or RDP connection from same source IP)
3. EDR detects outbound data transfer to an external IP from same source IP

All three stages must occur in order within 30 minutes, correlated by
source.ip. This pattern represents a complete intrusion lifecycle spanning
two products (EDR + NDR), from credential harvesting through exfiltration.
rules.name: Cross-Source Attack Chain - Credential Theft to Lateral Movement to Data Exfiltration
Cross-Source Credential Theft to Lateral Movement to Exfiltration

rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
Detects a DLP removable media event (sensitive data copied to USB) on a
machine where the user authenticated with a different account than their
usual pattern. This combination suggests a compromised account being used
to exfiltrate data via physical media — a pattern common in insider threat
and advanced persistent threat scenarios.
rules.name: DLP + Windows - Sensitive USB Copy with Unusual Authentication
DLP + Windows Compromised Account Exfiltration Correlation

rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
Correlates akeso_edr behavioral detections (shellcode injection, suspicious
process behavior) with Akeso AV static scan results on the same host.
When both the EDR rule engine and AV scanner independently flag activity on
the same host within 5 minutes, confidence is significantly higher than
either detection alone.
rules.name: EDR + AV - Behavioral Detection Confirmed by Static Analysis
EDR + AV Behavioral Static Confirmation Correlation

rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
Detects a credential theft alert from akeso_edr followed by a DLP
policy violation on confidential data by the same user within 30 minutes.
This pattern indicates a potential compromise → data theft chain where
stolen credentials are used to access sensitive files.
rules.name: EDR + DLP - Credential Theft Followed by Sensitive Data Access
EDR + DLP Credential Theft Data Access Correlation

rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
Detects a complete attack lifecycle spanning all Akeso products:
1. EDR detects lateral movement to a target host
2. AV detects a dropped malicious tool on the target host
3. DLP detects sensitive file access on the target host
4. EDR detects outbound data transfer from the target host

This four-stage sequence within 60 minutes on the same host represents
a high-confidence, complete intrusion — from initial access through
data exfiltration. Each stage is independently detected by a different
product, providing defense-in-depth visibility.
rules.name: Full Chain - Complete Attack Lifecycle Across All Products

rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
Four-stage cross-product temporal correlation spanning all major product types:
1. NDR detects SMB file transfer to a target host
2. AV detects the transferred file as malicious on the same host
3. EDR detects the process that dropped/executed the malicious file on the same host
4. Windows Event Log shows the user account that launched the process on the same host

All four stages must occur in order within 45 minutes, correlated by host.name.
This represents a complete lateral tool transfer scenario where an attacker moves
malware via SMB, it gets flagged by AV, EDR captures the execution chain, and
Windows auditing identifies the responsible user — four independent products
converging on one incident.
rules.name: Four-Source Attack Chain - SMB Transfer to Malware to Process Drop to User Login
NDR SMB File Transfer to Host
AV Malicious File Detection on Host

rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
NDR detects C2 beaconing to an external IP followed by EDR process creation
events on the beaconing host within 5 minutes. Correlated by host.name to
identify the responsible process for the beacon traffic.
rules.name: NDR + EDR - Network Beacon Followed by Process Identification
EDR Suspicious Process on Beacon Host
NDR Beacon to EDR Process Identification Correlation

rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
EDR detects LSASS access on Host A followed by NDR detecting SMB lateral
movement from Host A to Host B within 30 minutes. Correlated by source.ip.
Indicates credential theft leading to lateral movement via SMB.
rules.name: EDR + NDR - Credential Theft Followed by Lateral Movement
EDR Credential Theft to NDR Lateral Movement Correlation

rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
DLP classifies files on Host A as confidential followed by NDR detecting
high-volume outbound transfer from Host A within 60 minutes. Correlated
by host.ip and user.name. Confirms data exfiltration by linking DLP
content classification with NDR network behavior evidence.
rules.name: NDR + DLP - Network Exfiltration with DLP Confirmation
DLP Classification to NDR Exfiltration Correlation

rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
Full kill-chain correlation across NDR and EDR: (1) NDR detects port scan
reconnaissance, (2) EDR detects credential dumping on compromised host,
(3) NDR detects SMB lateral movement, (4) NDR detects high-volume outbound
data exfiltration. Correlated by user.name within 2 hours. Links network
recon, credential theft, lateral movement, and data theft into a single
high-confidence incident.
rules.name: NDR + EDR Full Attack Chain - Recon to Exfiltration
Full Attack Chain Correlation - Recon to Exfil

rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
NDR detects an SMB file transfer to a new internal host followed by AV
detecting the transferred file as malicious on the destination host
within 10 minutes. Correlated by destination.ip. Indicates lateral tool
transfer where an attacker moves malware between hosts via SMB.
rules.name: NDR + AV - Lateral Tool Transfer Followed by Malware Detection
NDR SMB Transfer to AV Malware Detection Correlation

rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
Alerts on any file flagged as malicious or suspicious by AkesoAV,
regardless of the specific signature or malware family. This is a
catch-all rule to ensure no AV detection goes unnoticed in the SIEM.
rules.name: Any Malware Detected by Antivirus

rules.author: AkesoSIEM
rules.description:
Alerts when AkesoAV quarantines or blocks a file in real-time,
indicating active threat prevention on the endpoint.
rules.name: File Quarantined or Blocked by Antivirus

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)
rules.description:

antivirus, indicating active adversary C2 infrastructure.
rules.name: Cobalt Strike Beacon Detected

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)
rules.description:

immediate incident response action.
rules.name: Ransomware Detected by Antivirus

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)
rules.description:

indicating active compromise on the endpoint.

channels, violating data protection policies.

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)
rules.description:

on Linux systems.

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)

security best practices and may indicate unauthorized access.

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)

commonly used for phishing and malware distribution.

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)

exfiltration or unauthorized bulk data movement.

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)

control beaconing or persistent backdoor connections.

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)

indicator of macro-based malware execution.
rules.name: Command Prompt Spawned by Office Application

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)
rules.description:

credential dumping attempts.
rules.name: Suspicious LSASS Process Access

rules.description:
Detects execution of mimikatz.exe, a well-known credential dumping tool
commonly used by attackers for lateral movement and privilege escalation.

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)
rules.description:

for persistence and privilege escalation.
rules.name: Scheduled Task Creation via Schtasks

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)
rules.description:
Detects execution of whoami.exe, often used by attackers for initial
reconnaissance after gaining access to a system.
rules.name: Whoami Reconnaissance Command

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)
rules.description:
Detects WMIC being used to create processes, often leveraged for
lateral movement and remote code execution.
rules.name: WMIC Remote Process Creation

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)
rules.description:
Detects creation of new user accounts which may indicate an attacker

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)
rules.description:

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)

movement or unauthorized remote access.

persistence mechanisms or malicious service creation.
rules.name: New Service Installed

rules.author: AkesoSIEM (SigmaHQ)

persistence mechanism for malware.
